merger_description:
Southern Cross Electrical Engineering Limited (**SCEE**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued shares in Entire Operations Pty Ltd (**Entire**) (the **Acquisition**).

The Acquirer, SCEE, is the ultimate holding company of the SCEE corporate group (**SCEE Group**). SCEE Group provides specialised electrical, instrumentation, communications, security, fire protection and maintenance services and manufactures electrical infrastructure products across Australia.

SCEE Group supplies these services and products to customers in the mining and resources, industrial, utilities, energy and renewables, transport infrastructure, healthcare, education, data centre, retail, commercial-building and residential-development sectors.

Relevant to the Acquisition, SCEE Group, through its subsidiary Force Fire Holdings Pty Ltd, supplies fire protection services in NSW and Queensland.

Entire is a provider of mechanical heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning services, as well as fire protection services, operating across a broad range of commercial, social infrastructure and transport infrastructure markets.

Relevant to the Acquisition, Entire supplies fire protection services in Victoria and Queensland. Entire has also occasionally undertaken work in NSW.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is limited geographic overlap between SCEE and Entire
in the supply of fire protection services across Australia
b. the parties’ combined share in the supply of fire protection
services in Queensland is estimated to be low and the
increase in share of supply arising from the Acquisition is
expected to be small
c. there are alternative suppliers of fire protection services in
Queensland.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
